That gap should be framed as unknown coverage requiring explicit disclosure, not as a failure and not as silently covered by general readiness evidence. It does permit certification when general readiness evidence supports launch readiness and the named-context evaluation gap is explicitly disclosed as a material limitation or coverage gap. Policy therefore distinguishes between noncompliant silent certification and compliant caveated certification.
